title: How the Zscaler Terraform providers store, log, and send secrets

prose.text: Provider credentials for the SDK itself are covered in [[shared.sdk-go.auth-lifecycle]]; this subject is about secrets that pass through resources and data sources. Secrets can show up in three different places when a Terraform provider handles a credential: in the state file, in plan and CLI output, and in logs. The `Sensitive` flag on a schema attribute affects how Terraform displays the value in plan and CLI output, and whether it changes what is written to state or to a provider's own log lines is open {{gap:sensitive-flag-scope}}.

c2c-ir-secrets-not-sensitive.statement: The ZIA `zia_dlp_cloud_to_cloud_ir` data source declares the nested `tenant_authorization_info` attributes `client_secret`, `user_pwd`, `secret_token`, `access_token` and `bot_token` as plain Computed strings. Unlike the provider's own `client_secret` argument, the schema does not set `Sensitive` on them.

"tenant_authorization_info": {
	Type:        schema.TypeList,
	Computed:    true,
	Description: "Tenant authorization information",
"client_secret": { Type:          schema.TypeString, Optional:      true, Sensitive:     true,

upstream.note: Filing 9 (credential handling) of the 2026-08 provider audit.

c2c-ir-secrets-copied-to-state.statement: The same data source's flattener copies the secret-bearing members of the API response (`client_secret`, `secret_token`, `user_pwd`, `org_api_key`, `cred_json`, `credentials`, `access_token`, `bot_token`) into those attributes, so whatever the API returns for them is written into the data source's state.
c2c-ir-secrets-copied-to-state.conditions: State receives these values only if the API actually returns them populated on read (gap api-returns-secrets).

upstream.note: Filing 9 (credential handling) of the 2026-08 provider audit.

c2c-ir-entity-log-includes-secrets.statement: The same data source logs `resp.OnboardableEntity` with `%+v`. That value is a pointer to a struct that holds `TenantAuthorizationInfo` by value, whose string members include `ClientSecret`, `SecretToken` and `UserPwd`, so the formatted line prints the secret-bearing members' contents. The line is prefixed `[DEBUG]` and has no redaction.
c2c-ir-entity-log-includes-secrets.conditions: Appears in output only when the provider's debug-level log output is enabled (the line carries a `[DEBUG]` text prefix; how that maps to a visible level is not shown here) and when the API returned the values (gap api-returns-secrets).

upstream.note: Filing 9 (credential handling) of the 2026-08 provider audit.

c2c-ir-response-log-prints-pointer-only.statement: The line above it logs the whole response with `Retrieved cloud-to-cloud IR: %+v`. In the SDK's response struct, `OnboardableEntity` is a pointer field.

quotes: ID                       int                      `json:"id,omitempty"` Name                     string                   `json:"name,omitempty"` Status                   []string                 `json:"status,omitempty"` ModifiedTime             int                      `json:"modifiedTime,omitempty"`

c2c-ir-response-log-omits-secrets.statement: So that line does not print the secrets: `%+v` prints a pointer field nested in a struct as an address, not the value it points to.
c2c-ir-response-log-omits-secrets.conditions: Rests on Go's fmt formatting, which prints the top-level pointer as &{...} but nested pointer fields as addresses; no vendor source states it.

cloud-nss-and-admin-token-in-state.statement: Two more ZIA data sources export credentials as plain Computed strings and write them to state: `zia_cloud_nss_feed` (`authentication_token`, `client_secret`; defined in `data_source_zia_cloud_nss_server.go`) and `zia_admin_users` (the `token` inside `exec_mobile_app_tokens`).

"client_secret": { Type: schema.TypeString, Computed: true, Description: "Client secret applicable when SIEM type is set to S3 or Azure Sentinel",
if err := d.Set("exec_mobile_app_tokens", flattenExecMobileAppTokens(resp)); err != nil {

cloud-nss-and-admin-token-in-state.conditions: State receives these only if the API returns the values on read (gap api-returns-secrets). Data source name corrected from zia_cloud_nss_server, which is not registered: provider.go registers dataSourceCloudNSSFeed as zia_cloud_nss_feed.

upstream.note: Filing 9 (credential handling) of the 2026-08 provider audit.

zia-data-source-secret-attributes-unmark.statement: No ZIA data source schema marks any of the secret-named attributes above `Sensitive`. Searching the ZIA data sources for attribute names containing secret, password, pwd, passphrase, token, api_key, psk, private_key, cred_json or credentials finds these unmarked instances: the Cloud-to-Cloud IR authorization attributes, `zia_cloud_nss_feed` `authentication_token` and `client_secret`, and `zia_admin_users` `token`. The matches that are not secrets (such as `is_password_login_allowed`) are ignored. A name search also misses values that can carry secrets under other names, such as the cloud NSS server's `connection_headers`.
zia-data-source-secret-attributes-unmark.conditions: Absence claim from a search at tf-zia v4.8.3: `git grep -n -i -E '"[a-z_]*(secret|password|pwd|passphrase|token|api_key|psk|private_key|cred_json|credentials)[a-z_]*": *\{' v4.8.3 -- 'zia/data_source_*.go'`, with `git grep -n 'Sensitive: *true'` returning, among data sources, only `pre_shared_key` in `data_source_zia_location_management.go`. Attribute-name matching misses secrets with other names, and the search covers v4.8.3 only. The list names every unmarked secret attribute found, not every secret the API can return. Data source name corrected from zia_cloud_nss_server to the registered zia_cloud_nss_feed (zia/provider.go).

upstream.note: Filing 9 (credential handling) of the 2026-08 provider audit.

zia-psk-handled-differently.statement: The ZIA data sources are not uniform. In `zia_location_management` the nested `pre_shared_key` is marked `Sensitive: true`. In `zia_traffic_forwarding_vpn_credentials` the `Sensitive: true` line is commented out, and so is the line that would set `pre_shared_key` from the response, so that data source declares the attribute but does not populate it.

quotes: "pre_shared_key": { Type: schema.TypeString, Computed: true, Sensitive: true, },

pra-create-sanitizer-mutates-request.statement: `zpa_pra_credential_controller` create expands the configured secrets into the request struct, then calls `sanitizeFields(&req)` before sending it. `sanitizeFields` writes the literal `***REDACTED***` into the request's string fields whose lowercased name contains `password` or `passphrase`. The mutated struct is what is passed to `pracredential.Create`, so the create request carries the sentinel in `password` and `passphrase` instead of the configured values (including when those fields were left empty in the configuration).
pra-create-sanitizer-mutates-request.conditions: What the ZPA API stores when it receives the sentinel (reject, or accept as the secret) is server behavior (gap api-pra-sentinel).

upstream.note: Filing 9 (credential handling) of the 2026-08 provider audit.

sanitizer-misses-private-key.statement: The sanitizer compares the lowercased Go field name with `private_key`, but the struct field is `PrivateKey`, which lowercases to `privatekey` and does not contain `private_key`. So on create the SSH private key is not replaced: it is sent as configured, while `password` and `passphrase` are replaced.

quotes: Description: "The SSH private key associated with the username for the login you want to use for the privileged credential",

upstream.note: Filing 9 (credential handling) of the 2026-08 provider audit.

pra-create-log-prints-private-key.statement: The create path logs the request after sanitizing it, with `%+v`. Because the sanitizer leaves `PrivateKey` unchanged, that INFO log line contains the SSH private key in clear text when one is configured, while `password` and `passphrase` show the sentinel. The line is logged on every create, at INFO level.

quotes: log.Printf("[INFO] Creating credential controller with request\n%+v\n", req)

pra-create-log-prints-private-key.conditions: Depends on the provider's log output being enabled for that line (the INFO-prefixed line is written by the standard logger; how Terraform surfaces it is not shown here), and on the private key being set.

upstream.note: Filing 9 (credential handling) of the 2026-08 provider audit.

pra-update-omits-empty-secrets.statement: On update the provider expands the secrets with `d.Get` and sends the PUT without sanitizing, so a changed secret is sent as configured. A secret that is empty in config becomes an empty Go string, and the SDK struct tags are `omitempty`, so the field is left out of the PUT body. An update cannot send an explicit empty value to clear a stored `password`, `passphrase` or `private_key`.
pra-update-omits-empty-secrets.conditions: Whether the API clears a stored secret when the field is absent from a PUT, or keeps it, is server behavior (gap api-pra-empty-secret).

upstream.note: Filing 9 (credential handling) of the 2026-08 provider audit.

pra-read-never-sets-secrets.statement: The resource's read sets `name`, `description`, `credential_type`, `username` and `microtenant_id` and nothing else. The three secret attributes are `Sensitive: true` in the schema but are never refreshed from the API, so their state is whatever the configuration supplied. After a create that sent the sentinel, the next plan shows no difference for the secrets. Read does log the whole API response at INFO with `%+v`, which would print any secret the API returns (gap api-returns-secrets).

quotes: "password": { Type: schema.TypeString, Optional: true, Sensitive: true,

pra-read-never-sets-secrets.conditions: Absence search at tf-zpa v4.4.10 and HEAD: `git grep -n 'Set("password"\|Set("passphrase"\|Set("private_key"' <ref> -- zpa/resource_zpa_pra_credential_controller.go` returns nothing. That unset attributes keep their prior state value is Terraform plugin SDK behavior, not shown in this repository.

upstream.note: Filing 9 (credential handling) of the 2026-08 provider audit.

pra-data-source-password-declared-not-se.statement: The `zpa_pra_credential_controller` data source declares `password` as a Computed string without `Sensitive`, but its read never sets it, so the attribute is always empty. This is a missing output, and as written it keeps the password out of state. If it were set without also adding `Sensitive: true`, it would be a plain-text state value like the ZIA cases.

quotes: "password": { Type: schema.TypeString, Computed: true, Description: "The password associated with the username for the login you want to use for the privileged credential",

pra-data-source-password-declared-not-se.conditions: Absence search at tf-zpa v4.4.10 and HEAD: `git grep -n 'Set("password"' <ref> -- zpa/data_source_zpa_pra_credential_controller.go` returns nothing. The last sentence is a consequence of changing the code, not something the code does now.

upstream.note: Filing 9 (credential handling) of the 2026-08 provider audit.

sanitizer-call-sites.statement: `sanitizeFields` is called in two places in the ZPA provider: PRA credential create and PRA credential pool create. The update path of the PRA credential does not call it. In the pool, the request struct has no field whose name contains `password`, `passphrase` or `private_key`, so the call changes nothing there.
sanitizer-call-sites.conditions: Search at tf-zpa v4.4.10 and HEAD: `git grep -n sanitizeFields <ref> -- zpa` returns the definition in zpa/utils.go, `zpa/resource_zpa_pra_credential_controller.go:126` and `zpa/resource_zpa_pra_credential_pool.go:109`.

upstream.note: Filing 9 (credential handling) of the 2026-08 provider audit.

sdk-logs-full-bodies-when-enabled.statement: When `ZSCALER_SDK_LOG` and `ZSCALER_SDK_VERBOSE` are both true, the SDK dumps API requests including their bodies, and API responses, in full. The OneAPI client leaves the body out for sandbox (`/zscsb`) requests and for its token request, whose response it does not log. Up to Go SDK v3.8.52 the dumps redacted neither secret fields nor the Authorization header. From v3.8.53 (#468) the SDK masks the values of credential headers (`Authorization`, `Cookie`, `Set-Cookie` and others) in the dumps, but only the header block is masked: bodies are still logged unredacted. The ZIA provider builds against the masking SDK from v4.8.11 (SDK v3.8.54) and documents the masking from that version; the ZPA provider v4.4.14 builds against SDK v3.8.55. The ZIA and ZPA providers set both variables through `WithDebug` whenever `TF_LOG` is DEBUG or TRACE, so ordinary provider debug logging is enough on the OneAPI path. The dumps are taken from the outgoing request (`DumpRequestOut`) and the received response (`DumpResponse`), so they show what is on the wire.

sdk-logs-full-bodies-when-enabled.conditions: The dump lines are `[DEBUG]`-prefixed and the default logger drops them unless `ZSCALER_SDK_VERBOSE` is true; `WithDebug` sets both variables. The legacy ZPA client path does not call `WithDebug`, so there both variables must be set by hand. Response bodies contain secrets only if the API returns them (gap api-returns-secrets). Changed upstream in Go SDK v3.8.53 (checked 2026-10-18): previously "When `ZSCALER_SDK_LOG` and `ZSCALER_SDK_VERBOSE` are both true, the SDK dumps every request including its body, and every response, in full, with no redaction of secret fields or of the Authorization header." (the rest of the statement is unchanged).

upstream.note: Filing 9 (credential handling) of the 2026-08 provider audit.

pra-create-dump-shows-sent-secrets.statement: With the SDK dumps on, a PRA credential create dump shows the request body as sent: the `***REDACTED***` sentinel in `password` and `passphrase`, and the configured `privateKey`. A read dump shows any credential the API returns.
pra-create-dump-shows-sent-secrets.conditions: Needs both SDK log variables true, which the ZIA and ZPA providers set through `WithDebug` when `TF_LOG` is DEBUG or TRACE on the OneAPI path. Request bodies are dumped unmasked in every audited SDK version, since the v3.8.53 masking covers only the header block. A read dump carries a credential only if the API returns it (gap api-returns-secrets).

api-returns-secrets.title: Whether the ZIA read APIs return secret values in clear
api-returns-secrets.blocks: saying that Cloud-to-Cloud IR, Cloud NSS and admin-user secrets actually reach state or logs, rather than only being exposed if returned
api-returns-secrets.detail: The provider copies whatever the SDK struct decodes. The sources do not say whether the ZIA API masks, omits or returns these fields on GET. Test in a scratch tenant: create a Cloud-to-Cloud IR, a Cloud NSS server with an authentication token and an admin with an Executive Insights token, read each through its API, and note whether the secret members are present in clear, masked or absent.

api-pra-sentinel.title: What the ZPA API does with the literal ***REDACTED*** in a PRA credential create
api-pra-sentinel.blocks: saying whether a PRA credential created through the provider is unusable, rejected, or stored with the sentinel as its secret
api-pra-sentinel.detail: The provider sends the sentinel in `password` and `passphrase`. Nothing captured says whether ZPA validates, rejects or stores it. Test in a scratch tenant by creating a credential with the provider and then checking whether a console session using it authenticates.

api-pra-empty-secret.title: What the ZPA API does when a PRA credential PUT omits a secret
api-pra-empty-secret.blocks: saying whether removing a secret from configuration clears it in ZPA or silently keeps the old value
api-pra-empty-secret.detail: The provider omits empty secrets from the PUT body. Test in a scratch tenant by updating a credential with a password to one without and reading it back for a changed state, and by using the credential.

sensitive-flag-scope.title: Whether the Sensitive flag changes what reaches state or provider log lines
sensitive-flag-scope.blocks: saying that marking an attribute Sensitive keeps its value out of state or logs
sensitive-flag-scope.detail: Unverified statement: The Sensitive flag does not change what is written to state or to a provider's own log lines. The flag is a Terraform plugin-SDK schema property documented as controlling display in plan and CLI output; no registered source in this repository states what it does for state storage or for log lines a provider writes itself. Read the Terraform and plugin-SDK documentation on sensitive values, or check a state file written for an attribute marked Sensitive.
